niche: a Dutch city's district heating company deciding in which heating season its west network's pump station first runs short on a design day once a housing corporation's 1970s flats leave their block gas boilers for the heat network in six phases across 2027 and 2028, each block's design-day circulation flow its design heat load over the temperature drop that connections heated by the same kind of installation make on cold days
answer: 2028-29 heating season (phases 1 to 6 need about 200 m3/h of design-day flow against 168 available at OS West, short by about 30; 2027-28 holds at about 150)
analyst_test: A strong planner who reads the capacity procedure, the hydraulic test, the rev2 heat-load study and the meter data correctly carries each converting block's design heat load into design-day flow at the network's 40 K design drop, the network's metered cold-day drop (39.7 K) or the drop of the network's pre-1985 buildings (33 to 42 K) and files none (the west station stays inside its 168 m3/h through 2028-29), when the blocks keep original radiators whose like connections run at about 24 K on cold days and put the station short in the 2028-29 season.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each connecting building's design-day circulation flow, its heat load over the supply-return temperature drop its installation makes, which a district heating planner sizes pumps on (flow equals load over 1.16 kWh per cubic metre per kelvin times the drop); with another field's nouns there is no supply and return temperature, no installation whose drop sets the flow, and no pump sized on that flow.
layer1: two reading systems: the drive-by system's monthly heat meter registers in GJ (older meters) or MWh until each meter's summer 2025 migration, the AMR feed's daily kWh and registers after; older meters exchanged for refurbished AMR meters at migration, newer ones fitted with a module
AMR days in UTC against the weather station's local days, and gas telemetry stamped in local time with its UTC offset across the clock changes
meter exchanges under one connection (summer 2026), the register's meter history mapping serials to connection numbers by date with the placement and removal readings
AMR communication gaps (rows absent, the first day back without a daily consumption) and temperature-log faults flagged G, all on days above 0 C
weather station daily means in tenths of a degree Celsius
the corporation's complex codes, the consultant's object names and WH codes, and the grid operator's EANs and boiler-room descriptions as three key systems
the consultant's concept (March 2026) and revision 2 (September 2026) heat-load studies overlapping
the grid operator's EAN re-registrations at a capacity change and its 2025-26 meter replacement programme, one resent telemetry read
stakeholder_role: the heat company's network capacity planner, who advises the executive team on the west pump station

spine.entity: one heat meter's reading for one UTC day

world.geography: Netherlands (a fictional city, its municipal heat company, a housing corporation and a 1970s neighbourhood; all names invented)

driver: A newcomer's draw on a shared carrier is its load over the drop it makes in the carrier, and the drop belongs to the equipment behind it, which the units already on the carrier show only as two regimes in their own readings that no field labels; carrying the newcomers at the carrier's design drop, its measured average or the average of similar-looking units finds room that is not there.
driver_concrete: Each converting block's design-day flow is its design heat load over 1.163 times the supply-return drop that the network's connections with original radiator systems make on days at or below 0 C (about 24 K, readable only as the high-return regime in the heat meters), not the network's 40 K design drop, its metered cold-day drop of 39.7 K or the pre-1985 buildings' 33 to 42 K, so OS West runs short in the 2028-29 season instead of never; a textbook 90/70 radiator drop of 20 K files 2027-28.
stump: A competent planner converts each block's design heat load into flow at the network's 40 K design drop, its metered cold-day drop or the pre-1985 buildings' drop and files that OS West never runs short through 2028-29; the step that lands it there is carrying blocks that keep their original radiators at a drop those radiators cannot make, when the network's own radiator connections, recognisable only by their high returns, run at about 24 K on cold days and put the station short in 2028-29.

differentiation.task140: task140 solves a compute pool's lowest-tier residual jointly with a dependent service whose load rises with that tier; task142 has no residual or dependency: each unmetered block's design-day flow is its load over the drop of its own installation, read from the metered connections whose cold-day returns show that installation, and the shared axes (objective gap, a unit swap, a capacity report) carry different mechanisms
differentiation.task134: task134 raises a held level's forward rate by the distance the untouched ground beside it shows; task142 has no held level or rate: it converts kilowatts to cubic metres an hour through a physical drop read from like installations on the same network
differentiation.task133: task133 lets each truck rise to the next binding limit in another dimension; task142 has no second limit: the one capacity is the station's flow, and the decisive estimate is the drop the unmetered blocks' radiators will make
differentiation.task167: task167 v2 matches a young grant book to the units whose first-year draws looked like its own and reads their schedule at later ages; task142's newcomers have no record at all: the blocks are unmetered, their installation is known from the works, and the parameter is a physical drop read from the metered connections whose cold-day returns form the high-return regime, with no age or schedule
differentiation.task261: task261 recomputes a subgroup difference's standard error over a design's replicates; task142 estimates no variance and compares no subgroups: it forecasts a station's design-day flow from a drop read off like installations
differentiation.task149: task149 v2 turns a census workplace tally into weekly trips at each workplace's own travel frequency read from a panel of workers' stays; task142 counts no trips and reads no panel: it converts unmetered blocks' kilowatts to cubic metres an hour through the drop of the metered connections that share their radiator installation

lineage.niche: a purchasing alliance of five Victorian public health services booking a private nursing provider's January to March 2027 Hospital in the Home overflow block, each member topped up in the alliance agreement's order to its 90th-percentile HITH visit requirement above its in-house nurses' capacity, when two members open a bone and joint infection at home pathway whose courses run for weeks
lineage.driver: The upper percentile of a period's total is set by how many of the units that generate it arrive and how long each one runs, so it has to be built from those units and their durations counted inside the window; treating the counted rows, or the weeks or months they fall in, as independent draws, or carrying a site's own past spread onto a planned mix that adds long-running units, understates it and misplaces every capped top-up.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each member's January to March 2027 HITH visits are the home days of patients admitted at random, each stream's stay set by its course (weeks for a bone and joint infection, days for cellulitis), so the 90th-percentile requirement is built from the plan's admissions by stream and the stays on file counted inside the quarter; a Poisson margin on the planned visits, or the spread of past weeks, months or quarters carried onto the plan, understates it, most at the two members opening the bone and joint infection pathway, and books the block in the wrong lots.
lineage.stump: A competent solver takes each member's planned visits as its expected requirement, adds the 90th-percentile margin of a Poisson count (or the spread of its past monthly visits) and books small lots spread across all five members; the step that lands it there is treating visits as independent counts when they arrive in admissions whose stays run from days to weeks, so the quarter's spread is the admissions' and their stays': built from them, the two pathway members need several lots each and the block runs out before the last member in the order.
lineage.answer: Northgate Health books 300 visits, Riverbend Health 250, Westmere Health 225, Kingsdale Health 75 and Hillcrest Health none: the 850-visit block runs out at Kingsdale
lineage.world: Australia, Victoria: Ironbark Health Alliance, Bellbird Home Nursing (Hospital in the Home overflow block)
